title: ee.preflight.guard.v1
description: Structured advisory risk-memory response emitted by `ee preflight check --cmd "<shell-command>" --json`. The report explains matching high-risk patterns and relevant memories with provenance, but ee never authorizes, denies, suppresses, or executes the inspected shell command. Process exit and exitCode are always 0 for a successfully generated report, including when destructive patterns match. This surface is intentionally not wrapped in the ee.response.v2 envelope; callers consume the structured advisory result directly.

schema.description: Pins the schema identity. Treat any other value as a contract drift.

command.description: The exact command string passed to `--cmd` (or the positional COMMAND arg).

exitCode.description: Process exit code for a successfully generated advisory report. Always 0; risk matches never become command denials.

checkedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which the advisory risk evaluation ran.

ruleId.description: Stable identifier for the matched rule (e.g. core.filesystem:rm-rf-root-home).

pattern.description: Pattern that matched the command string.

action.description: Advisory risk classification. Neither value suppresses command execution.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of why the rule fired.

recovery.description: Bounded next-step guidance for the matched rule.

source.description: Where this advisory rule came from (built-in registry vs. user/workspace rules).

resolution.description: Confirms that the advisory rule matched. The public CLI has no bypass, override, approval, allowlist, or command-authorization surface.

matches.description: Advisory rule matches with explainable classifications. Matches never change exitCode from 0.

memoryId.description: Stable memory ID of the matched record.

provenanceUri.description: Optional provenance URI for the matched memory.

severitySource.description: Where the severity was derived from.

matchedTerms.description: Terms from the command that matched memory content.

matchedMemories.description: Risk, failure, and anti-pattern memories that matched the command. Advisory CLI paths query workspace memories when a destructive pattern matches; this array is empty for ordinary commands or when no matching risk memories are available, in which case no_risk_memories appears in degraded[].

degraded.description: Degraded-mode signals from advisory pattern or memory retrieval. These signals never change exitCode from 0.
